summary: Priority-weighting config appears to cause 429s for concurrent low-latency sessions during bulk import windows
description:
Issue summary:
NimbusDocs reports spikes of 429 responses for realtime low-latency sessions (websocket and HTTP streaming) coinciding with scheduled bulk embedding imports. They observed that realtime connections that normally succeed at ~10ms token latency start receiving 429s once the bulk job begins to warm up.

Impact:
- Customer-facing search autocomplete degrades during daily import windows (10:00-11:00 UTC).
- ~20% of realtime sessions see 429s within first 60s of a bulk import starting.
- Customer is on a Dedicated pool; they expect isolation between realtime and bulk ingestion.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: ded-pool-09-us-east
- Region: us-east-1
- Traffic mix: 150 concurrent realtime streams (low token-rate), 40 parallel batch embedding workers (high token-rate).
- Config: route priority weights applied via console: realtime route weight=80, batch route weight=20 (customer configured), but autoscaler and rate-limiter logs indicate weight enforcement may differ.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start steady-state with realtime load: open 150 long-lived websocket streams that request streaming completions for short prompts every 30s.
2) Kick off the daily embedding backfill: 40 parallel workers each sending large batch requests (max_tokens ~ 4096, concurrency 4).
3) Observe within 30-90s that 429s appear on websocket starts and HTTP POSTs on realtime route.
4) Stopping the batch workers returns realtime success rate to normal within ~3 minutes.

Logs / sample responses provided by customer:
- "429: rate_limit_exceeded - tenant_quota_exhausted" (timestamped at import start)
- Trace ids: trace-77a4, trace-77a5, trace-77b1 (attached in customer zip)

Customer notes: they expected route priority weighting to guarantee realtime route tokens are preserved for low-latency sessions. They configured a separate route for realtime and selected "priority-weighting: strict" in the console. They suspect either: (a) priority weighting is not applied at the token-accounting layer, or (b) the autoscaler warm-up for batch workers consumes burst capacity causing short-term quota exhaustion.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Aisha Patel (customer): Opening ticket after observed 429 pattern during today's import window. Attaching sample traces and config export.

2026-03-09 - Support (Priya Singh): Thanks Aisha — we're triaging. Can you confirm if the batch workers use ephemeral API keys per worker or a single tenant key? Also please attach the route config JSON from the console.

2026-03-09 - Aisha Patel (customer): Batch workers use a pool of 10 short-lived keys (rotated hourly). Re-attaching route snapshot and autoscaler policy. We set realtime route as priority=high, strict=true.

2026-03-10 - Support (Priya Singh): Reproduced similar pattern on test harness with mixed traffic when using short-lived keys and autoscaler burst enabled. Filing follow-up to SRE. Linked SUP-71234 for related per-connection token bucket topic.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Marco Liu): Observed that token-accounting occurs at tenant-level before route enforcement; priority-weighting moves queue order but token counters are shared in the burst window. Posting preliminary hypothesis in #support and adding instrumentation to rate-limiter to log per-route accounting.

2026-03-12 - Support (Priya Singh): Collected additional logs from customer's pool and compared with our dev harness. Noted autoscaler warmup produced high short-lived per-host sessions that incremented tenant token counters before priority layer could preempt. Proposed workaround in comments below.

2026-03-12 - Customer (Aisha Patel): Thanks — we can try the suggested workaround (limit batch warmup concurrency) during next window. Also interested in a longer-term config that avoids manual coordination.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Instrumentation: enabled per-route token and per-tenant burst counters on ded-pool-09-us-east for next import window.

2026-03-10 - Finding: token consumption spikes from batch workers occur in <45s during warmup; tenant-level token bucket reaches burst capacity and returns 429s even though realtime queue should be prioritized at scheduling layer.

2026-03-10 - Root cause hypothesis: priority-weighting is implemented at scheduler/queue ordering but accounting for per-token quota happens at ingress before scheduler sees the request, so tenant-wide burst counters can be drained by rapid batch connection fanout (short-lived keys amplify this).
2026-03-11 - Corroboration: dev harness reproduced same symptom when using 10x ephemeral keys across workers; switching to shared worker key reduced 429 incidence by ~85% in tests.

2026-03-11 - Additional observation: autoscaler warmup policy had "pre-warm connections" enabled, which created synchronous connections that caused a short token surge by prefetching model context for each worker host.
resolution: Workaround applied 2026-03-12: advised customer to (1) set batch worker warmup concurrency cap to 4 per worker host, (2) switch to a shared worker API key for the immediate import window, and (3) disable pre-warm connections in autoscaler for the next job.
Result: customer reported realtime 429s dropped to <1% during the following import window and search latency returned to baseline within 90s of job start.

Longer-term action items: engineering to add per-route token reservation option (configurable) so dedicated pools can reserve guaranteed token capacity for high-priority routes. Tracking engineering request as INT-10234 (internal feature request).

Follow-ups: update documentation on mixed-workload guidance and add a console warning when enabling 'pre-warm connections' in autoscaler for pools with mixed high-priority realtime routes. See Confluence draft linked in related_confluence_pages.
Ticket status: awaiting engineering design and product guidance. Customer satisfied with workaround; set status to In Progress until feature/backlog item is scheduled.
